suppliedPromptOrKeyDefects.note: The smooth peg reaction is perpendicular to the rod. Take moments about A before resolving the forces. Using unrounded forces gives μ=0.622 to 3 significant figures; the supplied 0.621 is slightly inaccurate.
Take moments about the hinge, then resolve horizontally and vertically. The diagram places the wall to the right of the beam.
Recalculate the normal reaction after the pulling force is removed. Friction reverses only when the direction of motion reverses.
Find the speed when the rope snaps. Afterwards gravity and friction both decelerate the uphill sled, with the full normal reaction restored.
At the final limiting equilibrium, friction acts uphill and balances the downslope weight component. During ascent it acts downhill.

For downhill motion to restart, weight must exceed limiting friction. Use different acceleration magnitudes for ascent and descent. The supplied 6.34 s doubles the ascent time, but the return is slower; the total is 8.08 s.
The hanging mass descends and pulls P uphill. Combine the two equations of motion, with uphill friction acting on P.
At impending slip, the base moves away from the wall and the top moves down. Floor friction acts towards the wall; wall friction acts upwards. These directions give 0.603l, not the supplied 0.392l.
